mission.statement: To address the social, economic, educational, health, immigration, and cultural needs of Ethiopian immigrants in Greater Los Angeles - and to promote the cultural heritage of Ethiopia at large.

paragraphs: ECLA started in conversations between Ethiopian Angelenos who saw their neighbors falling through the cracks - language barriers at the DMV, parents unsure how to enroll a child, elders missing benefits they qualified for.

On September 28, 2019, those conversations became a town hall. By the end of the meeting, eleven volunteers had been elected to a founding board. Six months later, the pandemic arrived - and ECLA's first major work became bilingual health panels for community members navigating COVID in their second language.

timeline.body: Town hall meeting brings the community together to discuss forming an organization.
Eleven-member founding board elected. ECLA officially begins.
Operations shift virtual during COVID-19. Bilingual community health panels launch.
Subcommittees form. Programs expand to immigration, mental health, and youth.
Seven program areas serving Ethiopian families across Greater Los Angeles.

mission.statement: The Ethiopian Community Los Angeles, ECLA, is an inclusive, nonpolitical, and nonreligious civic organization aiming to address the social, economic, and educational needs of Ethiopian immigrants, and others in similar situations, residing in the Greater Los Angeles area of Southern California. ECLA is committed to promote the history and the cultural heritage of Ethiopia at large.

Six months later, the pandemic arrived - and ECLA's first major work became bilingual health panels for community members navigating COVID in their second language.
